acceptance: A durable readiness contract defines the smallest stable package-to-host boundary for the future package-owned subagent extension, including ownership, versioning, dependency, loading, trust, and failure decisions.

The contract preserves role-declared tool admission, task/configuration/context/tracer authority, evidence-validator isolation, Mermaid separation, explicit launcher loading, and project-trust boundaries without implementing a package move or runtime change.
The contract identifies exact implementation artifacts, focused validation, compatibility-shim removal conditions, recovery, residual risks, and explicit exclusions for a later implementation task.
Durable component navigation and changelog handoff identify this readiness result as a prerequisite for `package-owned-subagent-extension`.
